newsitem.title: USA: GM's Kokomo, Ind., plant seeks strike OK.
newsitem.headline: GM's Kokomo, Ind., plant seeks strike OK.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Kokomo, Ind., electronics plant may be the next facility to launch a local strike if United Auto Workers leaders grant a request made by workers on Thursday.
A spokeswoman for UAW Local 292 at GM's Delco Electronics unit in Kokomo said the local has sought strike authorization from the UAW's headquarers in Detroit.

A walkout at the facility would be particularly damaging to GM because it supplies all of the automaker's North American assembly plants with fuel system controllers, audio systems and other electronics.

"We're seeking permission to join other locals currently on strike," the spokeswoman said, adding that the union wants the walkout to pressure GM management into a new local labor agreement. The facility employs nearly 5,500 UAW workers.

So far, 9,809 GM workers have been idled because of strikes at GM's Indianapolis metal stamping plant and its Janesville, Wis., sport/utility vehicle plant. About 2,750 workers walked off the job at Indianapolis and 4,809 in Janesville. The strike also has forced GM to idle 2,250 at its Fort Wayne, Ind., truck plant due to parts shortages.
